Distribution functions for Continuous Dual-Process SDT (CDP)

Source: R/distributions.R
sdt_cdp_dist.Rd

Density and random generation for the continuous dual-process signal detection theory model (Wixted & Mickes, 2010). Two correlated continuous dimensions, Familiarity (F) and Recollection (R), generate the aggregate strength S = F + R that drives old/new confidence; Remember/Know judgments split "old" responses on R, and an optional Know/Guess split uses F. The response is a vector of counts across the response categories (multinomial likelihood), in the same format sdt_cdp() is fit to. See sdt_cdp() for the model and sdt_rating() when no R/K split is available.

Usage

dsdt_cdp(
  counts,
  stimulus,
  dfam,
  drec,
  thresholds,
  rcrit,
  kcrit = NULL,
  sigmar = 0,
  rho = 0,
  n_new = NULL,
  dist = "normal",
  log = FALSE
)

rsdt_cdp(
  n,
  n_trials,
  stimulus,
  dfam,
  drec,
  thresholds,
  rcrit,
  kcrit = NULL,
  sigmar = 0,
  rho = 0,
  n_new = NULL,
  dist = "normal"
)

Arguments

counts

Integer matrix with one row per observation and one column per response category in the canonical order new, [guess], know, remember (each block ordered by confidence; see sdt_cdp()), or a vector for a single observation. A data frame is read as the matrix of its rows. n_new + 2 * n_old columns (R/K) or n_new + 3 * n_old (R/K/G).

stimulus

Integer vector (0/1). Stimulus type: 0 = new/lure, 1 = old/target.

dfam, drec

Numeric vectors. Familiarity and recollection sensitivities: the target means on the F and R axes, each in units of the corresponding lure SD (both lure SDs are 1). They are component means of a bivariate latent space, not the balanced \(d_a\) that the other SDT models report as d – the old/new decision here is read off the aggregate strength S = F + R, so the model's discriminability is a derived quantity rather than either of these.

thresholds

Numeric vector of n_new + n_old - 1 ordered confidence thresholds on the aggregate F+R axis, or a matrix with one row per observation.

rcrit

Numeric vector. Remember criterion on the recollection axis.

kcrit

Know criterion on the familiarity axis. NULL (default), or a non-finite value for every observation, gives the R/K model; finite values for every observation give the R/K/G model. A kcrit with any non-finite element gives the R/K model for the whole call, also for the observations whose kcrit is finite, and warns when there are such observations. Every element counts, also one past the last observation: with one draw, kcrit = c(0.2, Inf) gives R/K and a warning. The length of kcrit sets the number of observations only when every element is finite (the R/K/G model): with one row of counts, kcrit = c(0.2, 0.3) gives two values and kcrit = c(0.2, Inf) one.

sigmar

Numeric vector. Log SD of the recollection target distribution (0 = SD 1).

rho

Numeric vector. F-R correlation on the unconstrained scale; tanh(rho) is the correlation. 0 (default) = independent processes (classic CDP).

n_new

Integer number of "new" confidence levels. Defaults to half the number of confidence levels, rounded down (so 3 of 7); the number of "old" levels follows as length(thresholds) + 1 - n_new.

dist

Noise distribution. Only "normal" is currently supported.

log

Logical; if TRUE return the log-density (default FALSE).

n

Integer. Number of observations to generate. n_trials, stimulus, thresholds, and the model parameters are recycled to this length.

n_trials

Integer vector. Number of trials per observation.

Value

dsdt_cdp returns the (log-)density (multinomial probability). rsdt_cdp returns an integer matrix with one row per observation and the canonical response count columns (new1, ..., remember<K>) that sdt_cdp() expects – cbind() it to a design data frame for a ready-to-fit data set.

Vector arguments

  • r*(n, ...) returns exactly n draws: a vector, or a data frame or matrix with n rows. Every per-observation argument (a parameter, a stimulus, a number of trials) is recycled to length n with rep_len(), as in stats::rnorm(): draw i uses element i, and a matrix is read element by element; only a set of values per draw, such as thresholds, takes row i of a matrix (see below). A shorter vector is repeated, also when n is not a multiple of its length. Until bmm 1.6.0 at the earliest, rddm() with n = 1 and parameter vectors still returns one draw per element, with a deprecation warning.

  • n is a single number of at least 0. A fraction is truncated, as in stats::rnorm(), and n = 0 gives an empty vector, or a matrix or data frame with zero rows and the usual columns. Unlike stats::rnorm(), which takes the length of a vector n, these functions stop on one; rddm() still takes its length, with a deprecation warning.

  • d*(x, ...) returns one value per observation: as many as the longest of x (its rows, when the observations are rows of counts) and the per-observation arguments, the others recycled to that length. Value i is what the call on the i-th elements alone returns. A matrix in an argument that takes one number per observation, such as x or d, holds one observation per element, as in stats::dnorm(). When x or any per-observation argument is empty, the result is empty, as in stats::dnorm(). A NULL argument, such as a misspelt column of a data frame, counts as empty, except where the default is NULL, as for criterion or kcrit: there it means that the argument is not given. Where an observation is a vector of counts (dsdt_rating(), dsdt_dpsdt(), dsdt_metad(), dsdt_ranking() and dsdt_cdp()), or the pair of mean_rt or var_rt values of dezdm(version = "4par"), a vector is always one observation: pass a matrix with zero rows for none, as an empty vector stops. An empty kcrit of dsdt_cdp() and rsdt_cdp() stops as well; kcrit = NULL gives the R/K model. Counts in a data frame, a tibble included, are read as the matrix of its rows, and so are mean_rt and var_rt of dezdm(version = "4par"). dsdm() with a data frame x is the exception: it returns a data frame of the same shape, one density per cell, and cuts longer parameters to the number of cells.

  • A set of values that describes one observation, such as the thresholds of the rating models, is a vector when every observation shares it and a matrix with one row per observation otherwise: row i belongs to observation i, or to draw i.

  • Configuration arguments such as version, dist, log, parametrization and n_new are single values and are never recycled. An argument that a version does not use, such as zr of dezdm(version = "3par"), is ignored.

References

Wixted, J. T., & Mickes, L. (2010). A continuous dual-process model of remember/know judgments. Psychological Review, 117(4), 1025–1054. doi:10.1037/a0020874

Examples

# CDP density (R/K, 1 new + 3 old levels: 3 thresholds, 7 count columns)
dsdt_cdp(
  counts = c(40, 5, 12, 30, 10, 18, 60), stimulus = 1,
  dfam = 0.8, drec = 1.0,
  thresholds = c(-0.5, 0.3, 1.0),
  rcrit = 0.7, n_new = 1
)
#> [1] 1.870555e-27
# Generate CDP count data (R/K, 3 new + 3 old levels) for 10 subjects
dat <- expand.grid(id = 1:10, stimulus = c(0L, 1L))
dat <- cbind(dat, rsdt_cdp(nrow(dat), 100, dat$stimulus,
                           dfam = 0.8, drec = 1.0,
                           thresholds = c(-1.1, -0.5, 0, 0.6, 1.3),
                           rcrit = 0.5, n_new = 3))
head(dat)
#>   id stimulus new1 new2 new3 know4 know5 know6 remember4 remember5 remember6
#> 1  1        0   13   16   14    16     5     5         8         9        14
#> 2  2        0   16   13   10    16     5     8         7        14        11
#> 3  3        0   26   17   14     8    11     1         1        11        11
#> 4  4        0   18   18   11    11     9     3         3         8        19
#> 5  5        0   19   11   12    16     9     5         6        11        11
#> 6  6        0   18    9   22    13    10     6         2         6        14
